title: Database connection pool exhausted
description: Production PostgreSQL database refusing new connections. Error: 'FATAL: sorry, too many clients already'. Users unable to log in.
resolution: Increased max_connections from 100 to 300 in postgresql.conf. Added PgBouncer connection pooling. Restarted database. All connections restored in 8 minutes.
root_cause: Sudden traffic spike during marketing campaign caused connection pool exhaustion. No connection pooler was in place.

title: Redis out of memory – cache eviction storm
description: Redis instance hitting maxmemory limit, causing aggressive key eviction. API response times spiked to 8s average. Cache hit rate dropped from 92% to 12%.
resolution: Attempted to increase Redis memory limit via CONFIG SET maxmemory 4gb. This temporarily resolved eviction but memory filled again within 30 minutes. Root issue unresolved – had to restart the job that was caching large objects.
root_cause: A new batch job was caching full API responses (5MB+) without TTL. Memory filled within 2 hours of deployment.

title: Kubernetes pod OOMKilled loop
description: Payment service pods continuously crashing with OOMKilled status. Pods restart every 2-3 minutes. Payment processing unavailable.
resolution: Increased memory limits in Deployment spec from 512Mi to 2Gi. Identified memory leak in transaction logging library (v2.3.1). Rolled back library to v2.2.9. Pods stabilized within 5 minutes of rollback.
root_cause: Memory leak introduced in transaction-logger v2.3.1. Memory accumulated until OOM killer triggered.

title: High CPU throttling on API nodes
description: All API nodes showing 98% CPU throttling. p99 latency increased from 120ms to 4200ms. Alert threshold exceeded for 15 minutes.
resolution: CPU limits in Kubernetes were set too low (500m). Attempted to increase limits but required node scaling first. Scaled node pool from 3 to 6 nodes. Redistributed pods. CPU throttling resolved in 20 minutes.
root_cause: CPU limits configured at 500m millicores were insufficient for the actual workload after a recent feature release doubled computational complexity of search queries.

title: Redis cache poisoning – stale data served
description: Users receiving stale pricing data for up to 2 hours after price updates. Cache TTL was set too high. Financial impact: $42,000 in incorrect pricing.
resolution: Flushed Redis cache with FLUSHDB. Reduced TTL for pricing keys from 7200s to 300s. Implemented cache invalidation webhook from pricing engine. Issue resolved but stale data impact persisted for users during the 2hr window.
root_cause: Pricing cache TTL was set to 2 hours. When prices were updated in the database, the cache was not invalidated. No cache invalidation strategy was implemented.

title: Database connection pool exhausted – second occurrence
description: Same PostgreSQL connection pool exhaustion as INC-001, but now with PgBouncer in place. PgBouncer itself is overloaded. max_client_conn exceeded.
resolution: Increased PgBouncer max_client_conn from 100 to 1000. Adjusted pool_size to 50 per database. Tuned server_idle_timeout from 600s to 60s. All connections restored in 5 minutes.
root_cause: PgBouncer's max_client_conn was set to default (100) – same as original DB limit. Traffic growth exceeded this limit.

title: Kubernetes pod OOMKilled – notification service
description: Notification service pods crashing with OOMKilled. Email processing queue backing up. 50,000 unprocessed notifications.
resolution: Increased memory limits from 256Mi to 1Gi. Did NOT roll back any library. Memory leak persisted. Pods crashed again after 2 hours. Eventually identified that large attachment payloads were being held in memory. Added streaming download and processing. Permanently resolved.
root_cause: Email attachments up to 200MB were being fully loaded into memory for processing. Memory limits (256Mi) were insufficient.

title: Cascading timeouts across microservices
description: Order service timing out, causing cascade failures in inventory, shipping, and payment services. Circuit breakers not triggering. 100% of checkout flows failing.
resolution: Identified slow database query in order service (full table scan, 45 seconds). Added EXPLAIN ANALYZE. Added index on orders.created_at + orders.status. Query time dropped from 45s to 12ms. Increased circuit breaker timeout thresholds. Services recovered in 8 minutes after index creation.
root_cause: Missing database index on frequently queried columns. A new reporting dashboard caused a full table scan query to run every 5 seconds.
